INFR.01.note: TeleGeography's continuously maintained FAQ explains fibre construction, routing, ownership, capacity, landing, repair, faults and why satellites carry only a small share of international traffic.

exercise.prompt: Use the submarine cable map to trace two independent routes between South Africa and Europe, then identify shared landing or geographic failure points.

INFR.02.note: DOE explains generation, transmission, substations and distribution, then shows why system operators must continuously balance real power to protect frequency and reliability.

deeper.title: Keeping the Lights On: Essential Reliability Services

exercise.prompt: Simulate a generator trip on a supply-demand graph and sequence inertia, primary frequency response, automatic control, dispatch and load shedding.

INFR.03.note: The Smithsonian account connects Malcolm McLean's experiment, intermodal transfer, port transformation, labour disruption and standard boxes as one system innovation.

article.title: Transforming the Waterfront
article.source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

exercise.prompt: Map one container from factory to customer, including stuffing, trucking, terminal gate, crane, vessel, customs, rail or road transfer, empty return and documentation.

INFR.04.note: CDC explains the conventional drinking-water train; EPA's municipal wastewater primer adds preliminary, primary, biological secondary and advanced treatment before discharge or reuse.

article.title: How Water Treatment Works
article.source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

deeper.title: Primer for Municipal Wastewater Treatment Systems

exercise.prompt: Draw the complete urban water loop from source through drinking treatment, distribution, household use, sewer collection, wastewater treatment, receiving water and possible reuse.

INFR.05.note: ICAO frames air traffic management as a total system combining airspace organization, communication, navigation, surveillance, separation assurance, collision avoidance and traffic-flow optimization.

exercise.prompt: Plan two crossing flights through controlled airspace and show how clearances, altitude, route, surveillance, handoffs, flow control and separation minima prevent conflict.

INFR.06.note: Nobel's account links Haber's catalytic ammonia synthesis to Bosch's engineering of a safe, durable high-pressure industrial process and large-scale fertilizer production.

exercise.prompt: Apply Le Châtelier's principle to nitrogen plus hydrogen forming ammonia and explain the engineering trade-offs among pressure, temperature, catalyst, conversion, recycle and energy use.

INFR.07.note: The American Cement Association separates cement from concrete and explains hydration, aggregate binding, placement, curing, strength development and durability.

exercise.prompt: Compare four mixes by water-cement ratio, aggregate, curing and reinforcement, predicting workability, porosity, compressive strength, cracking and embodied emissions.

INFR.08.note: WHO treats the cold chain as an end-to-end quality system involving forecasting, packaging, storage, transport, monitoring, stock control, equipment and contingency planning.

exercise.prompt: Design a cold-chain route to a remote clinic, including temperature range, packaging, data loggers, storage capacity, transport delays, power failure and product quarantine rules.

INFR.09.note: The U.S. Treasury's acquiring-service explanation clearly separates the real-time authorization message from later clearing, net obligations and interbank settlement.

article.title: How CAS Works
article.source: U.S. Department of the Treasury — Bureau of the Fiscal Service

exercise.prompt: Trace a card purchase through cardholder, merchant, gateway or processor, acquirer, network and issuer during authorization, capture, clearing, settlement and chargeback.

INFR.10.note: ISO explains standards as expert consensus that creates repeatable specifications, interoperability, safety, quality and access to markets rather than rules chosen by a single vendor.

exercise.prompt: Choose one everyday interface and list the dimensions, protocols, tests, terminology and governance that must be standardized for products from different firms to interoperate.

INFR.11.note: NIST describes the semiconductor supply chain as globally distributed, highly specialized and dependent on thousands of suppliers, with important geographic concentrations in tools and materials.

article.title: Vision for Success: Facilities for Semiconductor Materials and Manufacturing Equipment
article.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology

exercise.prompt: Map the supply chain for one advanced chip across design software, architecture IP, wafers, chemicals, lithography, fabrication, packaging, testing and final assembly, marking single points of concentration.

INFR.12.note: The NTP Project explains the hierarchy of reference clocks and servers, timestamp exchange, network-delay estimation, clock discipline, UTC and leap-second complications.

exercise.prompt: Record four NTP timestamps, calculate round-trip delay and clock offset, then explain asymmetry, drift, stratum, leap seconds and why monotonic time differs from wall-clock time.
